dimensions.note: No secret inputs or persisted command output; bounded failure excerpts redact common credential patterns and logs omit commands, paths, and output.
Every method logs entry and successful completion with structured non-sensitive status properties.
Validation, command, readiness, timeout, cancellation, and certificate failures throw before the single status resource write.
Seventeen synthetic tests cover success, malformed input, readiness and postcondition failures, timeout and cancellation cleanup, bounded output, and redaction.
Lifecycle commands are explicitly trusted supervisor-owned configuration and required to be idempotent; postconditions are verified before persistence.
No external provider API; optional HTTP health checks are syntactically loopback-only, redirect-disabled, deadline-bounded, cancellable, and retried.

Command duration and captured output are bounded; Linux process groups are terminated and streams settled on timeout/cancellation. The documented macOS detached-descendant limitation remains supervisor-owned.
README uses generic local examples and loopback addresses and explicitly documents additive Moment Savor integration rather than internal identifiers.
Global, nested, method, and output schemas are strict; authority is fixed to local-development and health URLs reject credentials/non-loopback hosts.
The sole status resource declares infinite lifetime and bounded garbage collection.
The generic local lifecycle is fully represented by start, stop, and status; process ownership deliberately remains with the configured supervisor.
Start and stop have a labeled policy check resolving and confining working directories to the Swamp repository tree.
Mechanical review confirms all three methods write the same six-field strict StatusSchema to status-current with complete 1:1 schema/write coverage and no caps or truncation.
Methods observe local supervisor and health state directly and do not read persisted resources.
This remains the first registry publication; there is no published model version or stored schema requiring migration.
